plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE (confounded batch, flagged)
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 lung RNA-seq samples (salmon-quantified raw counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples per profile note; matrix shape 12000x13 with the gene-symbol column) compare 6 treated vs 6 control samples. The metadata shows processing batch B1 holds all controls and B2 holds all treated samples — a perfect confound. Per the sourced rule (R-0005), a batch term cannot be fit and no batch-correction/SVA method can be applied without also removing the condition effect, since the design matrix would not be full rank. The plan therefore proceeds with a condition-only model, explicitly labels every downstream result as confounded (treatment effect is inseparable from batch/processing effect), and does not attempt ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or SVA. QC first characterizes whether PC1 tracks condition/batch (they are identical here) so the report can state this plainly rather than imply a clean causal claim. DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage is the primary DE call; edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs as a robustness cross-check, with the intersection reported as higher-confidence. Enrichment uses over-representation analysis (ORA) with an explicit tested-gene universe against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome pathway sets staged in the reference store (human, HGNC symbols) — the ranked/preranked GSEA method was rejected as a non-permitted enrichment method for this situation by the knowledge check, so ORA is used with the tested-gene universe and a fallback to a descriptive report if the significant gene list is too small (<50 genes) for the hypergeometric test to have power. All outputs carry the confounding caveat, package versions, and a reproducibility record.
